entries.english_v2: Sorry. Due to technical limits, you can't battle here yet...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the apology, the technical limitation, and the temporary unavailability of battles at this location.

entries.english_v2: The trade machine is broken too... Come back another time.
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps both the additional broken trade machine and the invitation to return later.

entries.english_v2: Hi there! May I help you?
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: Thank you! Please come again!
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: I'm raising Pokémon too! Once they get strong, no one will bully me anymore.
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves that the speaker also raises Pokémon and hopes their strength will put an end to the bullying.

entries.english_v2: If you need Poké Balls to catch Pokémon, get them at the Poké Mart!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the advice to buy Poké Balls at the shop specifically for catching Pokémon.

entries.english_v2: Raise Pokémon with care, and they'll grow close to you.
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly conveys that well-raised Pokémon become attached to their Trainer.

entries.english_v2: Flying is a little scary... but it gets you back to Pallet Town in no time.
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves both the fear of flying and its ability to return the speaker quickly to Pallet Town.

entries.english_v2: Bug-type Pokémon come in two kinds. Caterpie isn't poisonous, but Weedle is.
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the source's two Bug-type examples and its exact distinction between nonpoisonous Caterpie and poisonous Weedle.

entries.english_v2: I've never seen this Gym's Leader.
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology. Full-text review: Removes an unsupported claim that the Gym is always closed and translates the Chinese line directly.

entries.english_v2: Yes! I found a dragon bone!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the excited discovery and identifies the find as a dragon bone.

entries.english_v2: Potions are great! Use one when a Pokémon is low on HP.
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official Potion and HP terms while retaining when the medicine should be used.

entries.english_v2: Rattata may be small, but its front teeth are fierce!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps Rattata's small size and the contrasting power of its front teeth.

entries.english_v2: Viridian Forest is a natural maze. Be careful!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves Viridian Forest, its maze-like nature, and the warning to take care.

entries.english_v2: See those little trees by the road? A Pokémon move can cut them down.
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the roadside trees and the fact that a Pokémon's move can cut them down, unlike the unrelated 2015 Flash line.

entries.english_v2: Some Pokémon live only in forests or caves. Explore far and wide to find more!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the exclusive forest and cave habitats and the advice to travel more in order to find additional Pokémon.

entries.english_v2: Rocky caves are very dark. A Pokémon can light the way with Flash.
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the dark rocky cave and the use of a Pokémon's Flash move to see clearly.

entries.english_v2: Ah... These arcade games are so captivating...
entries.fidelity_comment: Restores the speaker's fascination with the game machines rather than the unrelated 2015 Pokémon friendship line.

entries.english_v2: The Bug Catchers in Pewter City are nothing like Brock at the Gym!
entries.fidelity_comment: Reviewed against the matching English Red/Blue/Yellow scene; the Chinese/Famicom wording is retained because the official line omits or contradicts a material source detail.

entries.english_v2: Keep wild Pokémon out of the flower beds!
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly retains the instruction not to let wild Pokémon enter the flower beds.

entries.english_v2: I got my Pokémon in a trade.
entries.fidelity_comment: Faithfully states that the speaker obtained the Pokémon by trading with someone else.

entries.english_v2: Some Pokémon won't obey you... A Badge would help!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the disobedient Pokémon and the source's suggestion that possessing a Badge would help.

entries.english_v2: It's $50 for a child's ticket. Would you like to come in?
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: Right! $50, please!
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: Come again!
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: We're going into space this month!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves both the planned journey into space and its timing this month.

entries.english_v2: If you catch more Pokémon than you can carry, use the PC to store them.
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the too-many-to-carry condition and the instruction to use the computer storage system.

entries.english_v2: You can carry up to six Pokémon.
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly preserves the carrying limit of six Pokémon.

entries.english_v2: I'm scared... I often hear strange sounds here.
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the speaker's fear, the repeated strange sounds, and this location.

entries.english_v2: Those poor people were robbed! We're sure Team Rocket did it. Even our Police Force has trouble with them!
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: You have Pokémon too? Train them well!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the surprised recognition that the player owns Pokémon and the advice to train them well.

entries.english_v2: Oh! Are you completing the Pokédex? That's great!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the question about completing the Pokédex and the speaker's enthusiastic approval.

entries.english_v2: Hi! Do you know how it feels to ride a Bicycle?
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly renders the greeting and question about the feeling of riding a Bicycle.

entries.english_v2: My bike is beautiful!
entries.fidelity_comment: Faithfully keeps the speaker's admiration for the appearance of their bicycle.

entries.english_v2: Team Rocket is making Pokémon dig holes. They must be up to something!
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains Team Rocket's use of Pokémon to dig and the suspicion that it serves a hidden purpose.

entries.english_v2: If we can't find what was stolen, we'll have to give up.
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the missing stolen property and the consequence that failure to recover it means giving up.

entries.english_v2: Sigh... Nothing has happened lately...
entries.fidelity_comment: Faithfully renders the sigh and the complaint that nothing has happened recently.

entries.english_v2: I just can't seem to raise my Bulbasaur properly...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the repeated difficulty the speaker has raising their Bulbasaur well.

entries.english_v2: Evolve your Pokémon to add more entries to the Pokédex...
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the connection between evolving Pokémon and increasing progress in the Pokédex.

entries.english_v2: I hear Ghost-type Pokémon have appeared in Lavender Town...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the rumor of ghost Pokémon appearing in Lavender Town, using the matching official place name.

entries.english_v2: This town is famous for its Pokémon graveyard. When Pokémon die, they're brought to Pokémon Tower.
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: Ghosts appeared in Pokémon Tower. I think they're the spirits of Pokémon that Team Rocket killed.
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: Do you believe in ghosts?
entries.fidelity_comment: Reviewed against the matching English Red/Blue/Yellow scene; the Chinese/Famicom wording is retained because the official line omits or contradicts a material source detail.

entries.english_v2: I can never forgive Team Rocket! They caught Cubone's mother as she fled and killed her!
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the speaker's anger and the full account that Team Rocket caught and killed Cubone's fleeing mother.

entries.english_v2: The city is under martial law!
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly preserves the current state of martial law rather than the unrelated 2015 command.

entries.english_v2: Many ghosts live in Pokémon Tower.
entries.fidelity_comment: Faithfully states that Pokémon Tower is inhabited by many ghosts.

entries.english_v2: Lavender Town's famous Pokémon Tower is a cemetery. People bring their departed Pokémon there to pray for them.
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: Mr. Fuji can soothe Cubone's spirit.
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the official matching identity Mr. Fuji for the Lavender elder and keeps his ability to comfort Cubone's spirit.

entries.english_v2: Those Team Rocket thugs are awful...
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly conveys the speaker's disgust toward the members of Team Rocket.

entries.english_v2: You're taking on Team Rocket? That's incredible!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the question about opposing Team Rocket and the speaker's admiration for doing so.

entries.english_v2: I saw Team Rocket's boss enter the building...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the eyewitness report that Team Rocket's leader entered the building.

entries.english_v2: I admire you! I'll be cheering for you!
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains both the speaker's admiration and promise of support.

entries.english_v2: I saw your battle. You're really strong!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the witnessed battle and the resulting praise of the player's strength.

entries.english_v2: Have you heard of Kameiyu from Nanjing Tech? They say all his Pokémon are as strong as Legendary Pokémon...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the Kameiyu and Nanjing Tech creator cameo and the rumor that his Pokémon have Legendary-level strength.

entries.english_v2: Welcome! Win coins in our games and trade them for the prizes you want. But it looks like you don't have a Coin Case...
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps earning coins through games, exchanging them for desired prizes, and the player's missing Coin Case.

entries.english_v2: I love games so much, I lost track of time...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the speaker's love of gaming and the resulting loss of awareness of time.

entries.english_v2: You want to play too? Sorry, you don't have a Coin Case.
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the desire to play and the explicit refusal caused by the missing Coin Case.

entries.english_v2: You can trade your winnings for Pokémon... Oh, but you don't have a Coin Case...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the Pokémon prize exchange and the fact that it is unavailable without a Coin Case.

entries.english_v2: Where'd that person go?
entries.fidelity_comment: The 2015 question matches the Chinese disappearance question; only its accidental missing word space was repaired.

entries.english_v2: When my Pokémon runs low on HP, I buy medicine for it at the shop.
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the Pokémon's depleted health and the speaker's response of buying medicine at the shop.

entries.english_v2: Hmm... There seems to be a basement under the Game Corner.
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the uncertain discovery of a basement beneath the matching official Game Corner location.

entries.english_v2: This really is a beautiful place!
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly conveys the speaker's admiration for the beauty of this place.

entries.english_v2: I won again today... Ha ha!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the speaker's latest victory, its timing today, and the laugh.

entries.english_v2: I wanted to put up a building here, but Pokémon attacked me!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the plan to construct a building at this spot and the Pokémon attack that interrupted it.

entries.english_v2: I hear the Elite Four at Indigo Plateau are very strong.
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the rumor about the Elite Four's strength and their location at Indigo Plateau.

entries.english_v2: The Chairman never stops talking about Pokémon...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the Chairman and his habit of talking endlessly about Pokémon.

entries.english_v2: Did you know Grimer is born from sludge in the sea?
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the question and the source's claim that Grimer originates in marine sludge.

entries.english_v2: The Safari Zone is home to many special Pokémon!
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly preserves the presence of many unusual Pokémon in the Safari Zone.

entries.english_v2: Strange... Where has my Pidgey flown off to this time?
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the speaker's puzzlement and the recurring disappearance of their Pidgey.

entries.english_v2: They say someone once saw a Legendary Pokémon in the Safari Zone...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the reported past sighting of a Legendary Pokémon inside the Safari Zone.

entries.english_v2: Do you watch TV often?
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly renders the question about frequently watching television.

entries.english_v2: How many Pokémon species are there in the world?
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the speaker's question about the total number of Pokémon species worldwide.

entries.english_v2: You want to beat this Gym...? You should give up.
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the player's intent to defeat the Gym and the speaker's discouraging advice to abandon the attempt.

entries.english_v2: The old master at the dojo is tough!
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly preserves the formidable old master and his association with the dojo.

entries.english_v2: Surprised? We've lived on this little island for years.
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the surprising fact that the group has lived on the small island for many years.

entries.english_v2: I feel so weak today... I'm exhausted...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves today's weakness and the speaker's extreme fatigue.

entries.english_v2: Fire-type Pokémon are in trouble against Water-types!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the source's unfavorable Fire-versus-Water type matchup.

entries.english_v2: Guests with rare Pokémon are welcome here!
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly preserves the welcome extended to visitors carrying rare Pokémon.

entries.english_v2: The fossil I found at Mt. Moon was brought back to life here!
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the fossil's discovery at Mt. Moon and its successful revival at this location.

entries.english_v2: Technology really has come a long way!
entries.fidelity_comment: Faithfully conveys the speaker's amazement at modern technological progress.

entries.english_v2: By the way, they say Eevee has more than three evolved forms...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves Eevee and the explicit rumor that its possible evolutions number more than three.

entries.english_v2: Hello, future Champion... Good luck!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the greeting, the player's future-Champion title, and the wish for good luck.

entries.english_v2: Every member of the Elite Four is tough. Be careful...
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the strength of all four Elite Four members and the warning to be cautious.

entries.english_v2: Dragon-type Pokémon are very strong... They have no weaknesses...
entries.fidelity_comment: Faithfully retains the Chinese source's explicit claim that Dragon-type Pokémon have no weaknesses.

entries.english_v2: Win, and you can enter the next room. Good luck!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps victory as the condition for entering the next room and the closing encouragement.

entries.english_v2: My grandfather at home wants to trade Pokémon.
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly preserves the grandfather at home and his wish to trade Pokémon.

entries.english_v2: A switch was activated!
entries.fidelity_comment: Faithfully reports that triggering the interaction activated a switch.

entries.english_v2: You don't want such a fine fossil?!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the surprised question about refusing a particularly good fossil.

entries.english_v2: Pokémon are not good or evil. It depends on their Trainer!
entries.fidelity_comment: Uses the matching official English Red/Blue/Yellow scene as its primary voice while retaining Chinese-only facts and Famicom-specific terminology.

entries.english_v2: Many people in the world use Pokémon for evil. Those scoundrels are Team Rocket!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the existence of people who misuse Pokémon and explicitly identifies the villains as Team Rocket.

entries.english_v2: Prices are too high, and no one will do anything about it. Sigh!
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the complaint about excessive prices, the lack of anyone willing to intervene, and the final sigh.

entries.english_v2: Even Pokémon at the same level can differ in strength.
entries.fidelity_comment: Directly preserves the claim that equal-level Pokémon need not have equal strength.

entries.english_v2: Higher-level Pokémon are stronger, but every type has opponents it struggles against...
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains both the strength gained with levels and the unfavorable opponents created by type matchups.

entries.english_v2: Got the Mystic Ticket!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves receipt of the special voyage ticket and keeps Mystic Ticket consistent with the matching earlier acquisition and boarding dialogue.

entries.english_v2: You never know when a Pokémon might leap out of the tall grass.
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the uncertainty and the sudden appearance of Pokémon from the grass.

entries.english_v2: Visit a big city, and you'll meet many skilled Trainers.
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the advice to visit a large city in order to encounter many excellent Trainers.

entries.english_v2: Have you been to Saffron City? I hear it has very tall buildings.
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves both the question about visiting Saffron City and the rumor about its tall buildings.

entries.english_v2: I want a Legendary Pokémon too, but where can they be found?
entries.fidelity_comment: Keeps the speaker's desire to own a Legendary Pokémon and uncertainty about where any can be found.

entries.english_v2: Judging by your skill, you must be a rookie Trainer. Always keep an eye on your Pokémon's condition!
entries.fidelity_comment: Preserves the assessment that the player is a novice and the advice to monitor their Pokémon's condition constantly.

entries.english_v2: With a Flying-type Pokémon, I could fly to faraway cities...
entries.fidelity_comment: Retains the Flying-type Pokémon and the wish to use it to reach distant cities by air.
